name: Schlieren
desc: Schlieren photography of an invisible medium — buoyant thermal plumes shed off pulsing burners and roll into turbulence, made visible only by their refractive-index GRADIENT as a knife edge at the focus cuts the deflected light into ghostly signed grey-on-grey; switchable to rainbow-filter schlieren, a caustic-edged shadowgraph, Mach-Zehnder interference fringes, or ironbow thermal.

energy.doc: schlieren sensitivity — how hard the density gradient is amplified into contrast (the master knob)

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the test section — guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: advection + field evolution rate (0.2 still flows)

density.doc: number, size and strength of the thermal sources feeding the plume

knife.doc: knife-edge orientation — which way a ray must deflect to be cut (rotates the light/dark relief); it also drifts slowly on its own

buoy.doc: buoyancy — from lazy stratified drift to a hard vertical chimney that shreds into vortices

hue.doc: primary hue of the faint duotone cast on the grey (and the rainbow filter's anchor)

x.doc: horizontal pan of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical pan of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: classic knife-edge grey schlieren / rainbow colour-filter schlieren / caustic-edged shadowgraph / Mach-Zehnder fringes / ironbow thermal

seed.doc: deterministic seed for source placement and the turbulent field
